svg.text: 1 · Request path 2 · What feeds what 3 · Shared folders. All public hosts are <name>.example.com; the drawings show only the name. Verified against the live systems on 14 Oct 2026.

g.data-desc: Open https://cloud.example.com/<app> from anywhere; Caddy answers with a 302 to the app's own host. The Homepage hub tiles and every Authentik launch URL use these cloud/<slug> links, so the family only ever types one address.

Immich, Home Assistant and Bitwarden apps log in through Authentik (OAuth / OIDC). KOReader (OPDS), Subsonic music players and CalDAV/CardDAV clients use per-app passwords on paths exempt from the SSO gate (/opds, /rest, /dav.php).
g.text: Immich · HA · Bitwarden · OPDS · Subsonic · DAV

g.data-desc: sslip.io names resolve to 192.168.10.20 without any DNS server and hit Traefik's LAN routers (plain http, or self-signed https). Seven apps also publish host ports that bypass Traefik and the SSO gate entirely: photos :2283, home :8123 (host network), mealie :9925, paperless :8012, homebox :7745, dav :6556, auth :9000 — plus the Runtipi dashboard on :80.

A Nebula node. From any network it reaches the lighthouse, CT 108 (10.42.0.11) and, through an unsafe_route via prox (10.42.0.10), the whole home LAN. The Nebula CA and the rebuild kit (~/heardos-install: scripts, compose overrides, Caddyfile copy) live here; secrets in ~/.config/credentials.env.
g.text: Nebula 10.42.0.20 · LAN route via prox · ssh · tipi.py · kit

g.data-desc: DNS only, nothing proxied: auth books budget cloud cron dash dav docs home homebox hub mealie music office paperless photos speed tube vault wallos. The apex and www point at a GitHub Pages site. mm (old Mattermost), dco and forge are leftovers pointing elsewhere. Records are managed with cfdns-add / cfdns-del on CT 108.
g.text: apex + www → GitHub Pages · stale: mm, dco, forge
VPS "nebula-lh" · 203.0.113.10 · Region-1 · the only public address · hourly billed

g.data-desc: Terminates TLS for every host, sets X-Forwarded-Proto https / Port 443, and reverse-proxies to 10.42.0.11:80 through the Nebula tunnel. No upload size cap (150 MB verified). cloud.example.com maps /<slug>/path → https://<host>.example.com/path for 22 slugs, including proxmox → https://prox.lan:8006 and runtipi → http://192.168.10.20 (LAN-only targets); unknown slugs go to the Authentik app library. Logs in journald.

Overlay 'example' 10.42.0.0/24. Nodes register here and traffic relays through it when a direct UDP path fails. Public port 22 is closed; SSH only over the overlay from certificates in group 'admins'.
g.text: UDP 4242 · relays when NAT blocks a direct path · ssh only from group admins
Nebula overlay 10.42.0.0/24 · encrypted node-to-node · .1 lighthouse · .10 prox · .11 CT 108 · .20 laptop
every node holds a certificate signed by the CA on the laptop; firewall rules are per certificate group (admins, servers, lighthouse)
PVE 9.2 · guests: LXC 108 + template 9000 · Zigbee dongle → CT 108 · web UI logs in with Authentik

g.data-desc: Proxmox VE 9.2. Guests: LXC 108 (the only one running) and a Debian 12 cloud-init template (9000). Its Nebula firewall lets group 'admins' reach local_cidr 192.168.10.0/24 and a NAT unit masquerades that traffic, so the laptop sees the whole LAN and the CT sees overlay clients as 192.168.10.2. The Sonoff Zigbee dongle (ZBDongle-E) is passed through to CT 108 by its /dev/serial/by-id path. The web UI (prox.lan:8006) logs in with Authentik (OpenID realm, app 'Proxmox VE', alice only).

g.text: LXC 108 "runtipi" · 192.168.10.20 · overlay 10.42.0.11 · Debian 12 · Runtipi v4 on Docker · 8 cores / 96 GB

g.data-desc: Runtipi's reverse proxy. Public routers (file provider, containers by name — never the Docker provider, which hides a router while its container is 'starting') receive Caddy's traffic; the CT's Nebula firewall allows tcp/80 only from the lighthouse group. LAN routers serve <app>.192-168-10-20.sslip.io; on Books and Music they strip every X-authentik-* header so nobody on the LAN can forge a login. Home Assistant is reached at 192.168.10.20:8123 because it runs on the host network.

g.text: public routers pub-<host> from Caddy (tcp/80 allowed only from the lighthouse) · LAN routers <app>.192-168-10-20.sslip.io · auth headers stripped on books & music

g.data-desc: Forward auth for the gated apps (embedded outpost; Traefik asks before every request and passes X-authentik-username) and OIDC provider for the self-login apps and Proxmox. Users: alice, bob (akadmin is the break-glass superuser). Access to each app = membership of its app-<slug> group; app-proxmox is alice only. Launch URLs point at cloud.example.com/<slug>. Brand 'HeardOS'.

g.text: forward auth for gated apps · OIDC for the rest and for Proxmox · users alice, bob · one app-<slug> group per app · launch URLs → cloud/<slug>
Gated · Traefik asks Authentik first, then forwards with the username header

g.data-desc: Plain-word tiles (Photos, Recipes & meal plan, Documents, Music, Videos, Passwords, Home controls, Paperwork, Where is it?, Subscriptions, My account, Books) linking to cloud.example.com/<slug>. Budget, cron, office, Runtipi and Proxmox are deliberately not on it.

Ebook manager (22 cookbooks, public 'Cookbooks' shelf). Logs you in from the Authentik header, trusted only from Traefik's network; /opds and /kobo are exempt so reader apps use a Calibre-Web password. Library: media/data/books.
Streams media/data/music (read-only mount), rescans every 15 min. Header login; /rest, /share and /backgrounds are exempt for Subsonic players, which need a Navidrome password.
YouTube front end with no login of its own, fully behind forward auth. No LAN route (https-only mode).

UI over root's crontab on the CT host; gate = forward auth, plus its own OIDC login. Jobs today: five ics-feed-* calendar imports (every 15 min), actual-to-wallos (06:10 daily), artcraft-repository mirror (every 2 h).

One-page family overview: this week's meals, open shopping lists, inventory, and the budget month once Actual's API password is enabled. Reads the Mealie, Homebox and Actual APIs, cached 3 min. No LAN route.

CalDAV/CardDAV. The admin UI is gated; /dav.php, /card.php, /cal.php and /.well-known are exempt and use Basic auth (Apple Calendar/Reminders, DAVx⁵, Home Assistant). Calendars: alice, bob, FamCal, Family Reminders, Meals, the public-feed calendars, and the Outlook work calendar imported into alice's own. Also on LAN port 6556.

Custom app. Browsers load the editor and its WebSocket from here, so the host is gated by Authentik forward auth (since 2026-10-14, proxy provider onlyoffice, group app-onlyoffice); the Nextcloud embed passes silently while your Authentik session is valid. Nextcloud ↔ Document Server traffic stays on the Docker network (http://onlyoffice/, StorageUrl nextcloud_migrated-nextcloud-1) and documents are additionally protected by the shared JWT. LAN name office.192-168-10-20.sslip.io.
LibreSpeed, public on purpose and stripped to just the test. It measures client → Region-1 → tunnel → CT 108, and anyone can burn VPS bandwidth with it.

g.text: Self-login · Traefik passes them straight through; the app signs you in with Authentik (OIDC)

g.data-desc: Photo library (16 GB in media/data/images/immich) with machine-learning, Postgres and Redis containers. Native OIDC including the mobile app's /api/oauth/mobile-redirect. Served via Caddy so uploads have no size cap. Also on LAN port 2283.

Family files, with OnlyOffice for in-browser documents (office.example.com, gated by Authentik + JWT). Mounts the other apps' folders as external storages — see table 3. LAN name nextcloud.192-168-10-20.sslip.io.
Recipes, meal plan and shopping lists. The meal plan becomes the 'Meals' calendar through a cron job; Home Assistant has a Mealie integration; the Dash reads the API. Also on LAN port 9925.

Scanned documents, local OCR, 16 category workflows; also holds the 22 cookbooks as type Book. Anything dropped into the consume folder (Nextcloud's 'Paperless inbox') is filed. Also on LAN port 8012.

Runs on the host network (port 8123). OIDC login via the hass-oidc-auth component. ZHA drives the Zigbee dongle (EmberZNet 8.0.3); CalDAV reads every Baïkal calendar and to-do list; plus Mealie, Apple TV, WiZ, Thread and mobile-app integrations.
Where things are. Registration is off; the Dash reads it through a dedicated service user's API key. Also on LAN port 7745.
Bitwarden-compatible vault, SSO only (password sign-up and sign-in disabled). Each user still sets a master password; the vault is end-to-end encrypted. Admin panel by token.

Recurring-cost tracker, filled every morning from Actual: monthly and quarterly payees in the Subscriptions and Bills & Utilities groups (10 today), priced at the latest charge, logos found online, stale ones marked inactive.
Envelope budgeting with SimpleFIN bank sync. OpenID-only login (sessions never expire); automation uses a session token. The first OpenID login became the owner; bob auto-creates as a basic user.

Installs and updates the apps (store slug 'migrated' plus custom apps cronmaster, dash, onlyoffice). Not public: the cloud/runtipi slug redirects to the LAN address and the Authentik 'Runtipi' entry is a bookmark. Driven from the laptop with tipi.py against its API.

g.text: installs/updates the apps · custom apps cronmaster · dash · onlyoffice · shared folders under /root/runtipi/media and app-data (table 3)
host ports go straight to the containers: no Traefik, no SSO
straight through · the app does OIDC with Authentik

g.data-desc: Reads the three APIs on each refresh (cached 3 min) and links every card back through cloud.example.com. The budget card waits on Actual's API password.

Example County and City of Springfield agendas, Smallville, the senior center, Discover Springfield, Historical Society, LocalVenue Historic Home, Riverland, Bruins, and the Outlook-published work calendar. The city's ICS export is broken server-side, so its agenda JSON is scraped instead.
Meal plan entries become the 'Meals' calendar (one all-day event per dinner, linking to the recipe). The Dash and Home Assistant's Mealie integration read it directly.
The actual-to-wallos job reads transactions with a never-expiring OpenID session token. The Dash's budget card still needs an API password (the server is OpenID-only).
Inventory totals, locations and recent items for the Dash, through a service user's API key.
The Paperless consume folder is mounted read-write as 'Paperless inbox': anything saved there is OCR'd and filed. Office documents open in OnlyOffice for editing.

Run as containers from root's crontab on the CT host. ics-feed-* (five jobs, one per feed): fetch, normalise, PUT one .ics per event into Baïkal, delete events that vanished upstream. actual-to-wallos: monthly/quarterly payees → Wallos subscriptions, idempotent via a marker in the notes. Logs appear in the CronMaster UI.
One read-only calendar per feed shared to the family; the Meals calendar; the work calendar written into alice's own. FamCal and Family Reminders are co-owned by alice and bob.
Ten subscriptions, matched by a marker in their notes so re-runs update instead of duplicating; stale payees are marked inactive, never deleted.
Edits Nextcloud documents in the browser. The public host is gated by Authentik forward auth; Nextcloud and the Document Server talk over the Docker network with a shared JWT.
Watches the consume folder; local OCR; 16 category workflows tag and type each document.
CalDAV integration (read-only service user 'homeassistant') exposes every calendar and to-do list; a Mealie integration shows the plan; ZHA runs the Zigbee network on the passed-through dongle.
Sends password-recovery links and admin notifications through Resend (smtp.resend.com:587, STARTTLS, send-only API key; DKIM signed with the apex domain, DMARC p=reject)
Passed from Proxmox into the CT by its stable /dev/serial/by-id path; EmberZNet firmware 8.0.3 since 2026-10-13.

g.text: Shared folders on LXC 108 (bind mounts, read from the running containers) · databases, keys and configs are never shared
